source_meta._title: Scroller in Telemetry Data screen renders translucent pixels as opaque, unlike elsewhere

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition client running snapshot 24w11a. Perform the reproduction from the title-screen menus; no world, server, game mode, commands, cheats, or operator permissions are required. Use the exact attached resource-pack archive transparent-scroller-test-24w11a-v1.0.zip and avoid other enabled resource packs that could override the same GUI texture.
preconditions: Install or create a Minecraft Launcher installation for Java Edition snapshot 24w11a.
Obtain the unchanged Mojira attachment named transparent-scroller-test-24w11a-v1.0.zip. Do not substitute a manually recreated texture pack unless the attachment is unavailable.
Keep the ZIP archive available to the operating system so it can be copied into the resource-pack folder.
Begin at the Minecraft Java Edition title screen.

Use a game window and GUI scale at which the Telemetry Data screen displays a vertical scroll bar. If the bar is not visible later, increase the GUI scale or reduce the game-window height and repeat the menu-navigation steps.

steps.action: Launch the Minecraft: Java Edition installation configured for the first affected version. Wait for the title screen to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The title screen is responsive and the displayed version text identifies the running version as 24w11a.

steps.action: On the title screen, click Options to open the game-options screen.
steps.success_cue: The Options screen is visible.

steps.action: Click Resource Packs to open the resource-pack selection screen.
steps.success_cue: The resource-pack screen shows Available and Selected pack lists.

steps.action: Click Open Pack Folder. Wait for the operating system's file manager to open the resourcepacks directory used by this 24w11a installation.
steps.success_cue: A file-manager window is open at the active Minecraft installation's resourcepacks directory.

steps.action: Copy the attached ZIP archive directly into the open resourcepacks directory. Leave it as a ZIP archive rather than placing it inside another folder.
steps.success_cue: transparent-scroller-test-24w11a-v1.0.zip is present directly inside the resourcepacks directory.

steps.action: Return to Minecraft. If the newly copied pack does not appear immediately, click Done to leave the resource-pack screen, reopen Resource Packs from Options, and wait for the pack list to refresh.
steps.success_cue: An entry corresponding to transparent-scroller-test-24w11a-v1.0.zip is visible in the Available list or is already present in the Selected list.

steps.action: If any unrelated custom resource packs are in the Selected list, move them back to Available by hovering over each pack icon and clicking its left-pointing removal arrow. Do not remove the built-in Default resources.
steps.success_cue: No unrelated custom pack remains enabled that could override the scroller texture.

steps.action: If the attached test pack is under Available, hover over its icon and click the right-pointing arrow to move it to Selected. Ensure the test pack is above Default in the Selected list.
steps.success_cue: The attached test pack's entry is in Selected above Default.

steps.action: Click Done to apply the selected resource pack. Do not continue while the resource-reload screen is active; wait until menu rendering has returned and mouse input responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Resource loading has completed and the Options screen is visible and responsive with the test pack enabled.

steps.action: From Options, click Language to open a deterministic comparison menu containing a scrollable list.
steps.success_cue: The Language screen is visible, with a list of languages and a vertical scroll control on the right side.

steps.action: Place the pointer over the language list and rotate the mouse wheel down by one notch, or drag the right-side scroll handle slightly downward. This establishes that a normal menu scroll control is present and usable without requiring selection of a different language.
steps.success_cue: The language list has moved slightly and the vertical scroll handle remains visible; the selected game language has not been changed.

steps.action: Click Done to return from the Language screen to Options.
steps.success_cue: The Options screen is visible again and remains responsive.

steps.action: Locate the button labeled Telemetry Data on the Options screen. Do not click it until the menu is fully responsive.
steps.success_cue: The Telemetry Data button is visible and ready to be activated.

steps.action: Click Telemetry Data once to open the Telemetry Data screen.
steps.success_cue: The game has begun displaying the Telemetry Data screen.

steps.action: Wait until the Telemetry Data title, data entries, and right-side vertical scroll control have all rendered. Do not leave the screen, change resource packs, or open another menu. If no vertical scroll control is present because the entire list fits, return to Options, increase GUI Scale under Video Settings or reduce the game-window height, and then reopen Telemetry Data.
steps.success_cue: The Telemetry Data screen is fully rendered and responsive, and its right-side vertical scroll control is visible with the attached test pack still enabled.

stor.handoff_condition: The attached translucent-scroller resource pack is active, and the Telemetry Data screen has just been opened and has finished rendering with its vertical scroll control visible. Begin visual observation without navigating away from this screen.
uncertainties: The contents and pack metadata of transparent-scroller-test-24w11a-v1.0.zip were not included in the supplied report text and could not be inspected directly; the reproduction depends on using the unchanged Mojira attachment.

The report does not identify which non-Telemetry scrollable menus were used for comparison. The Language screen is selected as a deterministic comparison because its list normally requires a vertical scroll control.

The report does not specify window dimensions or GUI Scale. These can determine whether a list requires scrolling, so the plan includes a conditional display adjustment only if the Telemetry Data scroll control is absent.
The report names the Telemetry Data menu but does not explicitly provide its parent-menu path. The plan uses the Options-screen Telemetry Data button available in the affected Java Edition UI.
Although a comment says the issue also affects '1.20.5 pre-release,' that version is not listed in the report's Affects versions field and is therefore not added to affected_versions.

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.20.4 client, using the attached resource pack in the single-player world-creation interface. No world, server, game mode, seed, coordinates, commands, or operator permissions are required for the selected superflat-customization reproduction path.
preconditions: Install or create a Minecraft Launcher installation for Minecraft: Java Edition 1.20.4, the first version listed as affected.
Obtain the Mojira attachment named "empty-slot-translucency-1.20.5pre1-v1.0.zip".
Keep the resource pack available as a ZIP file; do not manually edit its textures, metadata, or directory structure.

Ensure the test resource pack will have priority over any other custom resource pack that changes GUI or empty-slot textures. The simplest arrangement is to disable all other non-default resource packs.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation that uses Java Edition version 1.20.4 and start the game. Do not substitute the listed fix version 24w33a.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu has loaded, and the displayed version is 1.20.4.

steps.action: From the main menu, select the Options button.
steps.success_cue: The Options screen is open.

steps.action: Select Resource Packs to open the resource-pack selection screen.
steps.success_cue: The Resource Packs screen is visible, with available packs and selected packs shown in separate areas.

steps.action: Select Open Pack Folder. Wait for the operating system's file manager to open the resourcepacks directory used by this 1.20.4 game installation.
steps.success_cue: A file-manager window showing the active Minecraft resourcepacks directory is open.

steps.action: Copy the downloaded attachment ZIP into the open resourcepacks directory without changing its filename or contents. Return focus to Minecraft. If the pack does not appear automatically, leave and reopen the Resource Packs screen once to refresh it.
steps.success_cue: The pack from "empty-slot-translucency-1.20.5pre1-v1.0.zip" is displayed in the Available resource packs area.

steps.action: Activate the attached pack by hovering over or selecting its pack entry and clicking the right-pointing activation arrow, moving it from Available to Selected.
steps.success_cue: The attached pack is listed in the Selected resource packs area.

steps.action: If Minecraft displays a warning that the resource pack was made for a different game version, confirm that you want to use the pack. If no warning appears, continue without making another selection.
steps.success_cue: The warning, if presented, has been accepted and the test pack remains in the Selected area.

steps.action: If other custom packs are selected, disable them or use the pack-order controls to place the attached test pack above any pack that could override GUI textures.
steps.success_cue: The attached test pack is selected with no higher-priority custom pack capable of replacing its GUI or empty-slot textures.

steps.action: Select Done to apply the selected resource packs. Wait until resource reloading finishes; do not continue while the reload screen is displayed or the interface is unresponsive.
steps.success_cue: Resource reloading has completed and the responsive Options screen is visible again.

steps.action: Select Done on the Options screen to return to the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is visible and responds normally with the test resource pack active.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer.
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is open.

steps.action: Select Create New World. No existing world needs to be loaded or modified for this reproduction path.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Select the World tab in the Create New World screen.
steps.success_cue: World-generation settings, including the World Type control, are visible.

steps.action: Use the World Type control until its selected value is Superflat. Do not create the world.
steps.success_cue: The World Type control displays Superflat and the Customize button for superflat settings is available.

steps.action: Select the Customize button for the Superflat world type and wait until the Superflat Customization screen has completely rendered.
steps.success_cue: The Superflat Customization screen is fully visible, including its layer-list entries and their slot graphics, and the interface is responsive.

stor.handoff_condition: The attached resource pack is active, and the Superflat Customization screen has just finished rendering with its layer-list slot graphics visible. Hand control to the observation subsystem before closing the screen or changing resource packs.
uncertainties: The report provides several alternative viewing contexts: the Statistics item menu, the superflat customization menu, donkey/mule/llama inventory screens, and hovering over a bundle. This plan selects the superflat customization menu because it is explicitly supported by the report and requires no world creation, entity acquisition, inventory setup, or random exploration.

The attachment filename identifies 1.20.5 Pre-Release 1 even though 1.20.4 is the first affected version and therefore the required recommended version. The report instructs use of the attached pack and lists 1.20.4 as affected; Minecraft may consequently display a resource-pack compatibility warning when the attachment is selected in 1.20.4.

The report does not specify an operating system, launcher profile directory, UI language, GUI scale, graphics mode, seed, game mode, or server type. None is treated as a reproduction requirement for the selected menu-based path.

source_meta._title: Space characters at the end of a line in book and quill are invisible even if given a texture

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 24w45a, using the attached space-distinguisher-24w45a-v1.0.zip resource pack in a new disposable single-player Creative-mode world. No seed, coordinates, dedicated server, multiplayer session, commands, or non-default controls are required by the report.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher can install and launch the exact Java Edition snapshot 24w45a.
The Mojira attachment space-distinguisher-24w45a-v1.0.zip is available as an intact .zip file. Do not extract it before installing it as a resource pack.
Use a new disposable test world rather than an important existing world because the affected version is a snapshot.
Disable other non-default resource packs so that they cannot override the attached pack's modified space-character appearance.
A keyboard input method capable of entering an ordinary ASCII space character (U+0020) is available.

steps.action: Obtain the resource-pack attachment named space-distinguisher-24w45a-v1.0.zip from the report and retain it as a .zip file without extracting its contents.
steps.success_cue: The intact file space-distinguisher-24w45a-v1.0.zip is accessible from the operating system's file manager.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher and launch Minecraft: Java Edition using an installation configured for the exact snapshot version 24w45a. If no such installation exists, open the Installations tab, enable visibility of snapshot versions, create an installation whose version is snapshot 24w45a, and launch it.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft Java Edition 24w45a main menu is fully loaded and responds to input.

steps.action: From the main menu, open Options, then Resource Packs, and select Open Pack Folder to open this game installation's resourcepacks directory in the operating system.
steps.success_cue: The operating system displays the resourcepacks folder used by the running 24w45a client.

steps.action: Copy space-distinguisher-24w45a-v1.0.zip into the open resourcepacks folder. Leave the file zipped.
steps.success_cue: The zip file is present directly inside the resourcepacks folder.

steps.action: Return to Minecraft's Resource Packs screen. If the new pack is not listed immediately, leave and reopen Options -> Resource Packs once to refresh the list.
steps.success_cue: An available resource-pack entry corresponding to space-distinguisher-24w45a-v1.0.zip is visible.

steps.action: Disable any unrelated non-default resource packs, then activate the entry corresponding to space-distinguisher-24w45a-v1.0.zip by moving it from Available Resource Packs to Selected Resource Packs. Select Done to apply the selection.
steps.success_cue: The attached pack is in Selected Resource Packs, unrelated packs are disabled, and Minecraft has started applying the selected resources.

steps.action: Wait until resource reloading finishes. Do not proceed while a reload screen is present or the menu is temporarily unresponsive.
steps.success_cue: The reload screen has closed and the main menu responds normally.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set the game mode to Creative, and create the world. No particular seed or world-generation setting is required by the report.
steps.success_cue: The player has entered a new Creative-mode world.

steps.action: Wait until the loading-terrain screen has closed, nearby terrain has rendered, and player movement and menu input respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The world is fully interactive and surrounding chunks are rendered.

steps.action: Press the inventory action key, default E, to open the Creative inventory.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open, showing Creative item tabs and the player's hotbar slots.

steps.action: Open the Search Items tab, click its search field, and search for Book and Quill. Use the writable Book and Quill item, not a Written Book.
steps.success_cue: A Book and Quill item is visible in the Creative inventory search results.

steps.action: Place one Book and Quill from the search results into any hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: A Book and Quill is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Close the inventory using Esc or the inventory key, then select the Book and Quill's hotbar slot using its number key or the mouse wheel.
steps.success_cue: The world view is open and the Book and Quill is displayed as the currently selected hotbar item.

steps.action: Use the selected Book and Quill, using right-click by default, to open its writing interface. Do not sign the book.
steps.success_cue: The editable Book and Quill page is open with an active text-entry area and the Sign and Done controls visible.

steps.action: With the book's text-entry area focused, type the lowercase word test without punctuation or a trailing space yet. This is a deterministic substitute for the report's unspecified instruction to type 'something'.
steps.success_cue: The characters test have been entered on the current book page, and the book editor remains open.

steps.action: Immediately after the final t, press the Space key exactly once to enter one ordinary ASCII space character at the end of the current line. Do not type another character, change lines, select Done, or sign the book afterward.
steps.success_cue: One Space-key input has just been sent directly after test while the Book and Quill editor remains open and unchanged by any later input.

stor.handoff_condition: The Book and Quill writing interface is still open under the attached resource pack, and one ordinary space character has just been entered immediately after the text test as the final character on the current line. Begin observation before entering any additional character or closing the book.
uncertainties: The supplied report does not include the attachment's internal files or displayed resource-pack name; identify the pack entry by its association with space-distinguisher-24w45a-v1.0.zip. Reproduction cannot proceed if that attachment is unavailable because the modified visual appearance of space characters is essential to the test.

The report does not prescribe a game mode, world seed, server type, or item-acquisition method. A disposable single-player Creative-mode world is selected solely to obtain a Book and Quill deterministically without crafting or commands.
The report says to type 'something followed by a space' but provides no exact text. The string test followed by one U+0020 space is selected as a minimal deterministic input.
The report does not explicitly state whether other resource packs were active. Disabling unrelated packs is a practical isolation measure and is not asserted as a bug requirement.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-298982:TTF fonts cause z-fighting on signs with glow ink sacks | Relates:outward:MC-300693:Object text components on glowing signs render incorrectly
source_meta._title: Glyphs from TTF files are no longer rendered correctly on glow signs

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 1.21.5 using the report attachment font_from_ttf.zip as the active resource pack. Use a local single-player Creative-mode world as a deterministic way to obtain the required sign and glow ink sac; the report does not require multiplayer, a particular seed, coordinates, graphics settings, or a particular sign wood type. Disable unrelated custom resource packs to avoid font-provider conflicts.
preconditions: Minecraft: Java Edition release 1.21.5 is installed and selectable in the Minecraft Launcher.
The report attachments font_from_ttf.zip and sign_text.txt are available locally and have not been modified.
The operating system permits copying the resource-pack ZIP into Minecraft's resourcepacks folder.
The complete contents of sign_text.txt can be copied to the system clipboard.
No unrelated custom resource pack that replaces the same font glyphs is enabled.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher, create or select a Java Edition installation that uses release 1.21.5, and launch that installation. Do not select the listed fix version or a newer release.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft: Java Edition main menu is displayed and its version label identifies the running game as 1.21.5.

steps.action: From the main menu, open Options, then Resource Packs, and select Open Pack Folder. Leave Minecraft running while the operating-system file browser opens the resourcepacks directory.
steps.success_cue: A file-browser window showing Minecraft's resourcepacks directory is open.

steps.action: Copy the report attachment font_from_ttf.zip into the opened resourcepacks directory. Keep it as a ZIP archive; do not alter its files or add an extra enclosing folder.
steps.success_cue: font_from_ttf.zip is present directly inside the resourcepacks directory.

steps.action: Return to Minecraft's Resource Packs screen. If the pack is not yet listed, leave and reopen the Resource Packs screen. Find the pack corresponding to font_from_ttf.zip under Available, then click its icon or activation arrow to move it to the Selected side. Remove or deactivate unrelated custom packs that could override the same font glyphs.
steps.success_cue: The TTF test pack appears in the Selected resource-packs list, with no unrelated font-replacing pack selected above it.

steps.action: Select Done and wait for resource reloading to finish. Do not continue while the reload screen is visible or the menus are unresponsive.
steps.success_cue: Resource loading has completed and the main menu or Options menu responds normally.

steps.action: Return to the main menu, select Singleplayer, then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set Game Mode to Creative. Leave the seed and other world settings at their defaults; the report does not prescribe them.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Creative as the selected game mode.

steps.action: Select Create New World and wait until the player has entered the world, surrounding terrain has rendered, and movement and inventory input respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded Creative-mode world and can move normally.

steps.action: Press E, or the bound Open/Close Inventory control, to open the Creative inventory. Open the Search Items tab, search for Oak Sign, click the Oak Sign item to pick up a stack, and click an empty hotbar slot at the bottom of the inventory to place it there.
steps.success_cue: An Oak Sign stack is visible in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: While the Creative inventory remains open, use the Search Items field to search for Glow Ink Sac. Click the Glow Ink Sac item to pick up a stack, then place it in a different empty hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: A Glow Ink Sac stack is visible in a hotbar slot separate from the Oak Sign.

steps.action: Press E or Esc to close the Creative inventory. Use the number key corresponding to the Oak Sign's hotbar slot, or scroll the mouse wheel until the Oak Sign is the selected active item.
steps.success_cue: The hotbar selection outline surrounds the Oak Sign slot and the player is holding an Oak Sign.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the exposed top face of a nearby solid ground block and use the Place/Use Item control, right-click by default, once. This places a fresh standing sign and should immediately open its front-text editing screen.
steps.success_cue: A newly placed standing sign exists and the sign-editing screen is open for its front face.

steps.action: Outside Minecraft, open sign_text.txt and copy its complete contents without changing, retyping, translating, or reflowing the characters. Return to the sign editor, select the first text line, and paste using Ctrl+V on Windows/Linux or Command+V on macOS. Preserve any line breaks supplied by the attachment.
steps.exact_input: The complete, unmodified contents of sign_text.txt
steps.success_cue: The text from sign_text.txt is visible in the sign editor, including at least one character whose glyph is supplied or changed by the active TTF resource pack.

steps.action: Select Done in the sign editor to save the text and close the editor.
steps.success_cue: The world view is restored, the text is visible on the sign's front face, and the sign has not yet been treated with a glow ink sac.

steps.action: Confirm the TTF-font test precondition before triggering: keep the sign in view and verify that at least one pasted character is visibly rendered using a glyph changed by font_from_ttf.zip. If the characters are absent, shown as missing-glyph boxes, or unchanged because the pack failed to load, stop and correct the pack or text setup rather than applying the glow effect.
steps.success_cue: At least one target character is legible on the sign using the active resource pack's TTF-provided glyph.

steps.action: Use the appropriate number key or mouse wheel to select the hotbar slot containing the Glow Ink Sac.
steps.success_cue: The hotbar selection outline surrounds the Glow Ink Sac slot and the player is holding a Glow Ink Sac.

steps.action: Stand close enough to interact with the sign and aim the crosshair directly at the sign's front face—the same face displaying the TTF-rendered text. Do not interact yet.
steps.success_cue: The sign's text-bearing front face is within interaction range and centered under the crosshair while the Glow Ink Sac remains selected.

steps.action: Use the Place/Use Item control, right-click by default, exactly once on the text-bearing front face to apply the Glow Ink Sac. Do not click repeatedly or perform any further interaction before handing off.
steps.success_cue: One use-item input has just been sent to the sign's front face with a Glow Ink Sac selected.

stor.handoff_condition: The TTF resource pack remains active, the sign contains the unmodified text from sign_text.txt, and a glow ink sac has just been applied once to the sign's text-bearing front face. Hand control immediately to the observation subsystem without moving away, reopening the sign editor, changing resource packs, or applying another item.
uncertainties: The supplied raw report names font_from_ttf.zip and sign_text.txt but does not include their binary/text contents or direct attachment download data. The exact glyph sequence therefore cannot be reproduced in this plan; the executor must use the complete sign_text.txt attachment unchanged.

If the original attachments cannot be obtained, the report permits substitution with another resource pack that loads glyphs from a TTF file and any character specifically changed by that pack, but this is less deterministic than using the supplied attachments.

The report does not specify game mode, world seed, coordinates, sign wood type, operating system, graphics hardware, window resolution, or video settings. A local Creative-mode world and an Oak Sign are selected only to minimize unrelated setup.
The comments mention stronger visual problems at lower resolutions, but the formal reproduction steps do not require a particular resolution; this plan does not introduce one.
Web verification confirmed the standard Java Edition resource-pack installation and activation path, but the public issue page did not expose the attachment contents during verification.

source_meta._title: entity_data item component detection is broken in resource packs

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition client. Use 1.21.8 for the report's comparison run, followed by the first listed affected version, 25w34b, for the final reproduction. Use separate new single-player Creative-mode worlds with commands enabled. Enable the attached BrokenEntityDataExample.zip resource pack unchanged in both versions.
preconditions: The exact attachment BrokenEntityDataExample.zip has been downloaded and is available to the Minecraft client. Keep it as a ZIP file unless Minecraft fails to recognize it in that form.
Do not edit the resource pack's entity_data selector or apply the alternative selector syntax described in Mojira Comment 3; the attached pack must be tested unchanged.
The Minecraft Launcher can start the release 1.21.8 and the snapshot 25w34b. Snapshot versions are enabled in the launcher's installation-version filter if necessary.
Create a separate disposable world for each version. Do not open the 1.21.8 comparison world in 25w34b.
Use Creative mode and ensure commands are allowed so the supplied /give command can be executed from in-game chat.
The comparison run is performed first so the final trigger and handoff occur in the affected version 25w34b. This reverses the report's presentation order without changing either test condition.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Java Edition installation configured for version 1.21.8 and wait at the main menu. This is the comparison version named by the report, not an affected version.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left corner of the main menu identifies the running version as 1.21.8.

steps.action: From the main menu, open the resource-pack screen by selecting Options, then Resource Packs, then Open Pack Folder.
steps.exact_input: Options -> Resource Packs -> Open Pack Folder
steps.success_cue: The operating system opens the resourcepacks directory used by this Minecraft installation.

steps.action: Copy BrokenEntityDataExample.zip into the opened resourcepacks directory without changing the archive's contents or selector syntax, then return to Minecraft.
steps.success_cue: BrokenEntityDataExample.zip remains in the resourcepacks directory and Minecraft's Resource Packs screen is visible again.

steps.action: If the pack is under Available Resource Packs, use its arrow control to move it to Selected Resource Packs. Select Done and wait for resource reloading to finish. If it was already selected, leave it selected and choose Done.
steps.success_cue: The resource-pack screen closes, the main menu responds normally, and BrokenEntityDataExample.zip is enabled.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, configure the new world for Creative mode, ensure commands are allowed, and create the world. Give it a name that identifies it as the 1.21.8 comparison world.
steps.success_cue: A new 1.21.8 world begins loading in Creative mode with command access available.

steps.action: Wait until the player has entered the world, nearby terrain has rendered, and movement and input respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in the loaded 1.21.8 world without a loading overlay.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory action, whose default key is E.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open and displays item-category tabs and the player's hotbar.

steps.action: Open the Search Items tab, focus its search field, and search for item frame. Locate the ordinary item named Item Frame; do not substitute Glow Item Frame. Leave the search results visible briefly for the comparison setup, without evaluating the model result as part of this plan.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory search results include the ordinary Item Frame entry.

steps.action: Close the inventory using E or Esc so that in-game chat can be opened.
steps.success_cue: The inventory interface is closed and the normal world view is visible.

steps.action: Open in-game chat using the chat action, whose default key is T.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Do not rewrite its entity identifier, component syntax, capitalization, or NBT.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and one command-created Item Frame item is added to the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory again. Return to the Search Items tab and re-enter item frame if the previous search is no longer displayed. Keep the standard Item Frame search entry and the command-created item available as the completed 1.21.8 comparison state, but do not evaluate their model appearance in this setup plan.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is open, the ordinary Item Frame entry is present in the search results, and the command-created Item Frame is present in the player inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Close the inventory, open the pause menu, select Save and Quit to Title, and leave the 1.21.8 comparison world. Do not later load this world in the snapshot.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The client has returned to the 1.21.8 main menu and the comparison world is no longer loaded.

steps.action: Exit Minecraft, select the launcher installation configured for snapshot 25w34b, and start it.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and identifies the running version as 25w34b.

steps.action: Open Options, then Resource Packs. Verify that BrokenEntityDataExample.zip is under Selected Resource Packs. If it is only under Available Resource Packs, move it to Selected Resource Packs. Select Done and wait until resource reloading and menu responsiveness are complete.
steps.success_cue: BrokenEntityDataExample.zip is enabled unchanged in 25w34b and the main menu responds normally after resource reloading.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, configure a separate new world for Creative mode, ensure commands are allowed, and create it. Do not select or convert the previously created 1.21.8 comparison world.
steps.success_cue: A separate new world begins loading under 25w34b in Creative mode with command access available.

steps.action: Wait until the player has entered the 25w34b world, nearby chunks have rendered, and movement and controls respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in the loaded 25w34b world without a loading overlay.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory action, whose default key is E.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open.

steps.action: Open the Search Items tab, focus the search field, and search for item frame. Locate the ordinary Item Frame entry rather than Glow Item Frame. Do not evaluate its texture or model yet.
steps.success_cue: The ordinary Item Frame entry is visible in the Creative inventory search results in 25w34b.

steps.action: Close the Creative inventory using E or Esc.
steps.success_cue: The normal world view is visible and the player remains in the 25w34b Creative world.

steps.action: Open in-game chat using the chat action, whose default key is T.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept the supplied command.

steps.action: Enter the report's command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Do not replace the SNBT form, apply the workaround from Mojira Comment 3, or otherwise modify the command.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and one Item Frame carrying the supplied entity_data component is added to the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Immediately open the Creative inventory with E. Return to the Search Items tab and enter item frame again if the earlier query was cleared. Stop once the standard Item Frame search entry and the command-created Item Frame are available on the same inventory screen or between the search results and visible hotbar; do not evaluate their rendering.
steps.success_cue: The 25w34b inventory is open, the ordinary Item Frame entry is present in the Creative search results, and the command-created entity_data Item Frame is present in the player inventory or hotbar.

stor.handoff_condition: In the 25w34b Creative world, the unchanged BrokenEntityDataExample.zip pack is enabled, the supplied /give command has just created the entity_data Item Frame, and the Creative inventory is open with the ordinary Item Frame search entry and command-created Item Frame available for visual inspection. Hand control to the observation subsystem now.
uncertainties: The binary contents of BrokenEntityDataExample.zip were not included in the supplied text. This plan assumes the autonomous agent has access to the exact Mojira attachment and that the archive is not corrupted or renamed internally.

The report does not specify single-player versus dedicated server, a world seed, coordinates, or pre-existing world requirements. Separate new single-player Creative worlds are used as the minimum deterministic setup supporting Creative inventory access and the /give command.

The report presents the affected-version run before the 1.21.8 comparison. The plan performs the 1.21.8 comparison setup first so that the final trigger and handoff occur in the recommended affected version, 25w34b.

Resource-pack menu navigation and world-creation details are practical operational expansions and were not externally verified for these exact versions. No version-sensitive command or pack syntax from the report was changed.
